prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses was $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by provision expense of $4.7 million for the ACL on unfunded commitments related to the MidWest One acquisition.

The provision for credit losses is predominantly a function of Nicolet’s methodology and judgment as to qualitative and quantitative factors used to determine the appropriateness of the ACL. The appropriateness of the ACL-Loans is affected by changes in the size and character of the loan portfolio, changes in levels of collateral dependent and other nonperforming loans, historical losses and delinquencies in each portfolio segment, the risk inherent in specific loans, concentrations of loans to specific borrowers or industries, existing and future economic conditions, the fair value of underlying collateral, and other factors which could affect expected credit losses. The ACL for securities is affected by the risk of the underlying issuer, while the ACL for unfunded commitments is affected by many of the same factors as the ACL-Loans, as well as funding assumptions relative to lines of credit.

nonint.text:
Noninterest expense was $305 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $157 million (106%) over the comparable period of 2025. Personnel costs increased $51 million (60%), while non-personnel expenses combined increased $106 million (169%), primarily due to the acquisition of MidWest One .

Personnel expense was $136 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $51 million (60%) from the comparable period in 2025, reflecting a larger employee base due to the acquisition of MidWest One , as well as merit increases between the years.

Occupancy, equipment and office expense was $45 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up $18 million (64%) from the comparable period in 2025, mostly due to an expanded footprint resulting from the acquisition of MidWest One .

Data processing expense was $21 million, up $7 million (52%) between the comparable nine-month periods, mostly due to the MidWest One acquisition.

Intangibles amortization increased $12 million between the comparable nine-month periods due to increased amortization on newly established intangibles from the MidWest One acquisition.

Merger-related expense of $53 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily included compensation for severance and contract termination charges, as well as legal and professional expenses.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense was $37 million (effective tax rate of 21.3%) for the first nine months of 2026, compared to income tax expense of $26 million (effective tax rate of 19.3%) for the comparable period of 2025.

net.text: (1) The core net income and diluted EPS measures are non-GAAP financial measures that provide information that management believes is useful to investors in understanding our operating performance and trends and also aids investors in the comparison of our financial performance to the financial performance of peer banks. See section “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below for a reconciliation of these financial measures.

ocf.text: The $150 million decrease in cash and cash equivalents since year-end 2025 included $182 million net cash provided by operating activities (mostly earnings), $21 million net cash provided by investing activities (with net cash acquired from MidWest One and proceeds from investment sales, calls and maturities used to fund loan growth and new investment purchases), and $353 million net cash used in financing activities (mostly deposit declines, repayments of borrowings, and common stock repurchases). As of September 30, 2026, management believed that adequate liquidity existed to meet all projected cash flow obligations.

da.text: Preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying disclosures. Material estimates may be used in accounting for, among other items, the allowance for credit losses, valuation of loans in acquisition transactions, useful lives for depreciation and amortization, fair value of financial instruments, impairment calculations, valuation of deferred tax assets, uncertain income tax positions, and contingencies. These estimates and assumptions are based on management’s knowledge of historical experience, current information, and other factors deemed to be relevant; accordingly, as this information changes, actual results could differ from those estimates. Factors that may cause sensitivity to the aforementioned estimates include but are not limited to: external market factors such as market interest rates and employment rates, changes to operating policies and procedures, changes in applicable banking or tax regulations, and changes to deferred tax estimates.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: Tax-equivalent net interest income is a non-GAAP measure, but is a preferred industry measurement of net interest income (and its use in calculating a net interest margin) as it enhances the comparability of net interest income arising from taxable and tax-exempt sources. The tax-equivalent adjustments bring tax-exempt interest to a level that would yield the same after-tax income by applying the effective Federal corporate tax rates to the underlying assets. Tables 2 and 3 present information to facilitate the review and discussion of selected average balance sheet items, tax-equivalent net interest income, interest rate spread and net interest margin.

Noninterest income.heading: Table 4: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income was $94 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, $31 million (50%) higher than the comparable period of 2025, with growth in most core noninterest income categories primarily due to the acquisition of MidWest One . Noninterest income excluding net asset gains (losses) for the first nine months of 2026 was $93 million, a $31 million (50%) increase over the first nine months of 2025.

Wealth management fee income was $35 million, up $14 million (63%) from the first nine months of 2025, with growth in accounts and assets under management primarily due to the MidWest One acquisition.

Mortgage income includes net gains received from the sale of residential real estate loans into the secondary market, capitalized mortgage servicing rights (“MSR”), servicing fees net of MSR amortization, fair value marks on the mortgage interest rate lock commitments and forward commitments (“mortgage derivatives”), and MSR valuation changes, if any. Net mortgage income of $11 million increased $2 million (28%) between the comparable nine-month periods, mostly due to higher secondary market volumes and the related gains on sales.

intro.text: Nicolet Bankshares, Inc. (individually referred to herein as the “Parent Company” and together with all its subsidiaries collectively referred to herein as “Nicolet,” the “Company,” “we,” “us” or “our”) is a registered bank and financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the “Bank Holding Company Act”), and under the bank holding company laws of the State of Wisconsin. At December 31, 2025, Nicolet had total assets of $9.2 billion, loans of $6.8 billion, deposits of $7.7 billion and total stockholders’ equity of $1.3 billion. For the year ended December 31, 2025, Nicolet earned record net income of $151 million, or $9.78 per diluted common share.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
